sources.title: CAIIB Rules & Syllabus 2026
sources.document_date_basis: PDF creation metadata and the date in the file name; the title page says "Rules & Syllabus 2026"
sources.session_applicability: CAIIB 2026 (the page that links it lists the May/June 2026 and December 2026 examinations)
sources.note: Covers all four compulsory and all five elective papers. Syllabus on PDF pages 5-26.
established: PDF p.1: four compulsory papers and five electives; candidates choose one elective and may change it in any attempt.
PDF p.1: pass mark 50 out of 100 per subject; or at least 45 in each subject with 50% aggregate across all subjects in a single attempt.
PDF p.3: about 100 objective multiple-choice questions for 100 marks including case-based questions; the Institute may vary the number of questions.
PDF p.3: some numerical questions have no options and the answer is keyed in.
PDF p.3: online mode only; no negative marking for wrong answers.
PDF p.3: duration 2 hours.
PDF p.4: cut-off rule: exams held March to August use regulator guidelines and developments up to 31 December; exams held September to February use those up to 30 June.
PDF p.26: battery-operated portable calculator allowed, up to 8 functions and 12 digits; scientific calculators not allowed.
open_points: The illustrative cut-off table on PDF p.4 still shows 2025 sessions. The December 2026 cut-off (30 June 2026) is derived from the general rule on the same page, not from a 2026-specific table.
Six section headings are set in plain type and were inferred as headings (flagged on each topic). The extraction has not been proofread line by line by a person.

December 2026 session exam dates: 6 Dec (ABM), 12 Dec (BFM), 13 Dec (ABFM), 20 Dec (BRBL), 27 Dec 2026 (electives).

sources.title: Notice: Information and operational guidelines in respect of new set of questions 'Questions without options' from November/December 2023 CAIIB examination
sources.document_date_basis: date in the file name
sources.session_applicability: From the November/December 2023 CAIIB examination onward; no later replacement was found on the academics notice page on the retrieval date
established: Questions without options appear in all four compulsory subjects and carry one mark each.
Only digits, a leading minus sign and a decimal point can be keyed in; commas and other characters are not accepted.
Where the number of decimal places is specified, the answer is rounded to that many places (examples: 8.7678 to 8.77, 8.7623 to 8.76, 5.45678 to 5.4568).
An answer that is not saved is treated as not attempted.
open_points: The notice gives rounding examples but does not state a rule for an exact tie (a trailing 5). The app uses half-up rounding for authored answers and must avoid tie cases in questions until that is confirmed.

sources.title: Real Time Gross Settlement System (RTGS) FAQs
sources.document_date_basis: Date shown on the page
sources.session_applicability: Facts checked on the retrieval date; see the batch review for applicability at the 30 June 2026 cut-off.
established: RTGS: real-time, gross (no netting), settled in the books of the RBI, final and irrevocable; minimum remittance Rs 2,00,000 with no upper ceiling; available 24x7x365.

sources.title: National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) System FAQs
sources.document_date_basis: Date shown on the page
sources.session_applicability: Facts checked on the retrieval date; see the batch review for applicability at the 30 June 2026 cut-off.
established: NEFT: owned and operated by the RBI; batches at half-hourly intervals, 24x7x365; no RBI amount limit but a member bank may set limits with Board approval; non-account holders may remit cash up to Rs 50,000 per transaction; beneficiary credit expected within two hours of batch settlement.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Forthcoming Instructions) Directions, 2025, RBI/DoR/2025-26/173
sources.document_date_basis: Date of the Directions shown on the document
sources.session_applicability: The Directions state that their effective date of implementation will be communicated separately; no effective date was found. Until then the Basic Indicator Approach in the Capital Adequacy Directions applies. Later notification of an effective date was not searched for beyond the copy retrieved.
established: Chapter IV: the Basel III standardised approach for operational risk (business indicator, business indicator component with 12, 15 and 18 per cent coefficients at 8,000 and 2,40,000 crore, internal loss multiplier, loss component of 15 times average losses, loss data requirements); interim arrangement is the Basic Indicator Approach.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Asset Liability Management) Directions, 2025, RBI/DoR/2025-26/163
sources.document_date_basis: Date shown on the Directions; effective from the date of issue (paragraph 2)
sources.session_applicability: In force at the 30 June 2026 cut-off on its face; the copy read is a mirror of the 28 November 2025 text.
sources.note: PDF saved locally (not committed). Chapters III and VIII and Annex IV used; Chapters IV to VII (intraday, LCR, NSFR, interest rate risk) are left to later units.
established: Chapter II role of the Board; Chapter III governance, tolerance, flow and stock approach, monitoring, stress testing, contingency funding, overseas operations; Chapter VIII reporting periodicity; Annex IV Basel principles.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Climate Finance and Management of Climate Change Risks) Directions, 2025, RBI/DoR/2025-26/172
sources.document_date_basis: Date shown on the Directions; effective immediately (paragraph 2)
sources.session_applicability: The copy read is marked updated as on 1 October 2026 (after the 30 June 2026 cut-off); the only change noted is a substitution of the board committee wording effective 1 October 2026 (paragraphs 7 and 19), which does not affect the facts used. The Directions as read contain the green deposits framework only; they contain no provisions on assessing or managing physical and transition risk.
established: Definitions of green deposit, green finance and greenwashing; Board policy; rupee denomination; no differential interest; DICGC cover; financing framework; eligible categories and exclusions; third-party verification; impact assessment; review report.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Priority Sector Lending - Targets and Classification) Directions, 2025, RBI/FIDD/2024-25/128
sources.document_date_basis: Issue date; in force from 1 April 2025, replacing the 2020 Directions
sources.session_applicability: The page read is the consolidated text updated as on 11 September 2026 and lists Amendment Directions dated 19 January 2026 and 7 August 2026 (and a 25 August 2026 reference). The January 2026 amendment predates the 30 June 2026 cut-off; its content was not separately read, so only figures that are identical in the courseware and in the consolidated text (targets of 40, 18, 14, 10, 7.5 and 12 per cent for domestic banks) are used, and all limit-by-limit eligibility amounts are held back.
sources.note: HTML page saved locally (not committed); text extract at content/sources/primary/rbi-psl-2025.txt.
established: Paragraph 7.1 targets for domestic commercial banks: total priority sector 40 per cent of ANBC or CEOBSE whichever is higher; agriculture 18 per cent (14 per cent non-corporate farmers, 10 per cent small and marginal farmers); micro enterprises 7.5 per cent; weaker sections 12 per cent; UCB total 60 per cent; district weights 125 and 90 per cent from FY 2024-25.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Concentration Risk Management) Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/158 (copy shows Updated as on October 01, 2026)
sources.document_date_basis: Date of the Directions; the copy was updated on 1 October 2026
sources.session_applicability: Chapter III (Large Exposures Framework) paragraphs 4, 15, 16, 20, 25, 62-66, 79 read; the copy records the deletion with effect from 1 January 2026 of the Chapter IV framework for enhancing credit supply to large borrowers through the market mechanism, and inserts or deletes real estate and capital market paragraphs with effect from 1 October 2026 (after the cut-off); the paragraphs used are not marked as amended after the cut-off in the pages read.
established: Eligible capital base is Tier 1 capital; single counterparty limit 20 per cent plus up to 5 per cent by Board policy in exceptional cases; group of connected counterparties 25 per cent; large exposure 10 per cent or more; connectedness by control or economic interdependence; look-through threshold 0.25 per cent; single NBFC (excluding gold loan companies) 20 per cent; the large borrower market mechanism chapter deleted from 1 January 2026.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/164 (copy shows Updated as on October 01, 2026)
sources.document_date_basis: Date of the Directions; the copy was updated on 1 October 2026
sources.session_applicability: Paragraphs 5, 42-46, 80-96 read. The copy was updated after the 30 June 2026 cut-off; the amendments marked in the pages read concern paragraphs not used here (a deleted standard-asset sub-item and agricultural paragraphs). SMA (special mention account) categories are NOT in this document and were not retrieved.
sources.note: PDF saved locally (not committed). Text extract not committed.
established: Definitions of NPA, substandard, doubtful, loss, out of order, unsecured exposure; NPA triggers (90 days, out of order, 180 days limit review, crop seasons, derivatives); borrower-wise classification; provisioning for standard assets (0.25, 1.00, 0.75, 0.40 per cent), substandard (15, 25, 20 per cent), doubtful (100 per cent unsecured; 25, 40, 100 per cent secured by period) and loss assets (100 per cent).

sources.authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India
sources.title: Notification S.O. 1364(E) of 21 March 2025 amending S.O. 2119(E) of 26 June 2020 (classification of micro, small and medium enterprises)
sources.document_date_basis: Date of the Gazette notification
sources.session_applicability: In force from 1 April 2025, so in force at the 30 June 2026 cut-off on its face; later amendments were not searched for. The PDF (9 pages: Hindi then English text) contains the amending notification and the principal 2020 notification text, read in English.
sources.note: PDF saved locally (not committed). Text extract not committed.
established: Micro: investment in plant and machinery or equipment up to Rs 2.5 crore and turnover up to Rs 10 crore; small: Rs 25 crore and Rs 100 crore; medium: Rs 125 crore and Rs 500 crore; composite criteria; GSTIN units under one PAN counted together; investment linked to the ITR; exports excluded from turnover; Udyam registration on self-declaration.

sources.title: Lending to Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) Sector (Amendment) Directions, 2026, RBI/2025-26/206 of 9 February 2026
sources.document_date_basis: Date of the Amendment Directions
sources.session_applicability: Applies to loans to MSE borrowers sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026, before the 30 June 2026 cut-off.
sources.note: Only the quoted text of paragraph 4.1 and the effective date were read (via the page-reading tool); the local file is an extract of that text, not the notification PDF. The base Master Direction was not read.
established: Mandated collateral-free MSE loans up to Rs 20 lakh; discretionary extension to Rs 25 lakh on track record; gold or silver voluntarily pledged is not a violation; effective for loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026.
